children: said Tuesday it secured contracts valued at a combined €2.3B to supply trains for use on high-speed rail in Vietnam and to help Austria's railway company modernize the country's rail infrastructure.

said the up to €1B ($1.15B) agreement between its Siemens Mobility rail business and Vietnam's VinSpeed builds on an existing framework signed last year between the two parties; Siemens will serve as the technology partner under the deal, while VinSpeed — part of Vingroup, Vietnam's largest conglomerate — will build the tracks and handle the civil works.
Under the deal terms, Siemens Mobility
will deliver 10 of its Velaro Novo trains, a model that can reach speeds of 350 km/hour, and supply signaling and electrification systems, as well as technical expertise.
The company said is positioning itself as a leader in defining high-speed rail standards in Vietnam, laying the groundwork for the future long-distance network.

also said it was awarded a contract valued at ~€2.3B ($1.49B) to digitalize Austria's interlocking technology, part of a long-term framework agreement with a total volume of €2.6B to help Austria's railway company modernize the country's rail infrastructure.
The company said it will provide technology to integrate interlockings, train control system, and cybersecurity.

title: Siemens bags big new contracts in Vietnam and Austria worth €2.3B
